variants.note: own massing_affinities: massed-picturesque canonical, villa-tower canonical ('the tower at the reentrant angle holding the stair'). The dominant tower must rise at least one full storey above the main ridge (soft constraint c04).

CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from english-palladian ('the roof is never the composed feature... kept behind a parapet') -- contradicted by this style's own steep 45-55 degree slate roof (already correctly bound at family level in roof_pitch) and dominant tower massing.

roof_form.rule: A steep slate roofscape organised around a dominant tower rising at least one full storey above the main ridge (soft constraint c04) -- never a low roof hidden behind a classical parapet.

variants.note: defining_characteristics #6: 'Steeply pitched slate roofs with tall corbelled chimney stacks.' typical_ratios: 'Main roof pitch 45-55 degrees in slate.'
CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from mediterranean-vernacular -- has no place in this style, which names slate directly and repeatedly.

Hard co-occurrence constraint c02: 'Ornament is confined to the wall head -- corbel table, parapet, dormer heads, chimney caps. The lower two storeys must remain plain walling.' The eave itself carries none of the style's ornamental budget.

CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from regency, which explicitly pairs wide bracketed eaves with a shallow 22-30 degree roof -- Regency's own rule states outright that 'a steep roof under wide eaves belongs to the Italianate, forty years later,' and this style's own roof is steep (45-55 degrees), so the borrowed rule contradicts its own stated logic when applied here.

eave_condition.rule: The eave is minimal and unornamented; the style's entire ornamental budget is spent at the wall head above it (corbel table, parapet, dormer heads, chimney caps -- hard constraint c02), never on a bracketed eave overhang.

variants.note: defining_characteristics #3: 'Walls of squared rubble, granite ashlar or harled rubble, plain and unornamented through the lower storeys.'

CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved as an extends from english-classical+regency, whose own rule requires stucco 'ruled and lined to imitate ashlar' -- a smooth, jointed imitation-masonry finish that is the opposite of this style's genuinely rough squared rubble, granite ashlar or harl. Hard climatic constraint c05: 'Cement harl on a rubble wall fails in this climate faster than anywhere else in Britain' -- harl here means lime harl over real rubble, not a Regency stucco skin.

primary_cladding.rule: Squared rubble, granite ashlar, or lime-harled rubble -- plain and unornamented for the lower two storeys (hard constraint c02) -- detailed for driven rain: deep reveals, weathered copes, no exposed horizontal ledges (soft climatic constraint c05).

cornice.rule: CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from english-georgian as a classical modillion cornice. Directly contradicted by hard constraint c02: ornament is confined to the wall head (corbel table, parapet, dormer heads, chimney caps), and by governing_logic: 'None classical.' No classical entablature-derived cornice appears anywhere in this style.

variants.note: defining_characteristics #5: 'Ornament and incident concentrated entirely at the wall head: corbel tables, crenellated parapets with rounds, carved dormer pediments breaking the eaves.'

CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from regency, whose own rule states the parapet is used only 'where the roofline is not where this style spends its ornamental budget' -- the exact opposite of this style, whose own hard constraint c02 puts the ENTIRE ornamental budget at the wall head and parapet.

parapet.rule: A crenellated parapet with rounds (bartizans) is a primary carrier of the style's wall-head ornament (hard constraint c02) -- never shallow or plain.

variants.note: Hard co-occurrence constraint c03: 'openings are square-headed or, rarely, semicircular.' Reveals expressed at 300-450 mm (typical_ratios).
Hard constraint c03: 'Pointed arches, tracery and English bargeboards are forbidden.'

CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX (softened rather than forbidden): wrongly resolved from regency as the canonical form. Not wrong in outline (a plain surround is plausible) but the Regency reasoning ('never the deep keyed arch of the Baroque generation') is not this style's own; kept as atypical rather than forbidden since it does not contradict anything this style's own text states, but demoted because it is not documented here directly.

window_head_masonry.rule: Square-headed openings (rarely semicircular), set in deep 300-450 mm reveals expressing the wall's real thickness -- never a pointed arch (hard constraint c03).

special_window.rule: CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from english-palladian as a licensed classical Venetian/Diocletian window -- directly contradicted by governing_logic ('None classical') and hard constraint c03 (no classical apparatus among the openings).

door_surround.rule: CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved as an extends from english-classical+regency, supplying a baseless Greek Doric porch -- directly contradicted by governing_logic ('None classical') and hard constraint c03, which permits only square-headed or rarely semicircular openings and forbids classical apparatus throughout. No true classical order forms the entrance surround in this style; door treatment is plain walling consistent with the unornamented lower two storeys (c02).
door_surround.note: EDITORIAL: this node's own text does not itemize a specific door-surround device, so the correction removes a clear classical-apparatus error without asserting a fabricated replacement device.

transom_sidelight.rule: CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from adam-style as a delicate classical radiating fanlight -- directly contradicted by governing_logic ('None classical').

variants.note: No historical precedent. Absorbed into the plain, unornamented lower two storeys (c02) as one more plain wall opening, never competing with the wall-head ornament above it.

garage_strategy.rule: INVENTED, no historical precedent. A plain opening in the unornamented lower walling, consistent with the style's own wall-head-only ornament budget.

variants.note: defining_characteristics #5: 'carved dormer pediments breaking the eaves.' diagnostic_tells: 'Dormers rising through the eaves with carved and dated stone pediments, frequently initialled for the owner.'

CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved as an extends from antique-classical+english-palladian, a rigorous Palladian centrepiece-portico pediment rule with a rusticated basement this style does not have.

pediment.rule: Pediments occur only over dormers at the wall head, carved and often dated or initialled for the owner -- never as a proportioned classical portico centrepiece.

pilaster.rule: The inherited binding ('none... ornament goes to the iron balcony and bow') happens to reach the same outcome as this node's own governing_logic ('None classical'), but for Regency-specific reasons that do not apply here -- Baronial has no iron balcony tradition either. Restated on this node's own terms: no pilaster, and no classical order of any kind (governing_logic).

balustrade.rule: CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from regency as a cast-iron balcony rail -- this style has no ironwork-as-ornament tradition; its ornament is carved stone concentrated at the wall head (corbel table, crenellated parapet, dormer heads -- hard constraint c02), not a Regency balcony device.

ornament_vocabulary.rule: CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from regency as ironwork-as-principal-ornament. Corrected to the style's own documented vocabulary: carved stone concentrated entirely at the wall head -- corbel tables, crenellated parapets with rounds, carved and dated dormer pediments, chimney caps (hard constraint c02, defining_characteristics #5) -- with the lower two storeys deliberately plain.

ceiling_height_rule.rule: CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved as an extends from renaissance-classical/english-palladian, a Palladian arithmetic/geometric/harmonic-mean derivation 'checkable against a published plate' -- directly contradicted by this style's own governing_logic ('None classical') and its own description of plastered, comfortably-proportioned Victorian rooms with no plan-ratio derivation.

trim_family.rule: CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from english-classical, whose own note explicitly scopes the shared trim tradition to 'Baroque and Palladian rooms... core Georgian practice... Adam... Regency' -- this style is not named among them, and this node's own text describes plastered Victorian rooms with no reference to that graded classical continuum: 'the rooms are large, square, well-lit, plastered and comfortable, laid out with a Victorian sense of circulation.'
trim_family.note: EDITORIAL correction removing a misapplied borrowed rule; this node's own text does not itemize a replacement trim profile.

variants.note: own massing_affinities: villa-tower canonical, 'the tower at the reentrant angle holding the stair.' description.long: 'a rigorous Victorian service plan -- separate approach for the family, a servants' wing with a bell system, a business room next to the front door -- is wrapped in turrets and crow-steps.'

CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from english-classical, which forbids the very picturesque, asymmetrical-tower circulation this style's own massing_affinities and description document directly.

circulation_parti.rule: A stair tower at the reentrant angle organises vertical circulation, wrapped around a rational Victorian service plan (family approach, servants' wing, business room) -- the picturesque exterior and the ordered Victorian interior are two different arguments made by the same building.

glazed_area_pct_wall_max.note: Own hard-adjacent proportional constraint c04, more precise than the borrowed mediterranean-vernacular range.

daylight_strategy.rule: CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX (precision correction, not a reversal): the inherited mediterranean-vernacular figure (5-20% aperture, thermal-mass reasoning) happens to land near this style's own number but for the wrong climatic reason. This node's own soft constraint c04 states the number directly: glazed area not to exceed roughly 16 percent of elevation -- 'noticeably smaller in relation to wall area than any contemporary classical house' (typical_ratios), for defensive-derived proportion and Scottish weather, not Mediterranean sun-shading.

variants.note: description.long: the composition 'never resolves into a single frontal view, which is the picturesque intent.' Exemplar The Glen: 'a textbook Bryce composition of towers, turrets, crow-steps and corbelled dormers on a hillside site.'

landscape_idiom.rule: Sited to be read obliquely and in the round rather than frontally -- often on rising or hillside ground that lets the tower and silhouette be seen from below and to the side, the opposite of an axial approach.
landscape_idiom.note: EDITORIAL: inferred from the description and exemplar rather than a single explicit siting rule.
